title: Alejandro Fernández, Maná & More Set for Star-Studded Mexican Independence Day Las Vegas Lineup

Mexican Independence Day is celebrated on the evening of Sept. 15 to commemorate the Cry of Dolores, which re-enacts the speech given by Father Miguel Hidalgo in the historic early morning hours of Sept. 16, 1810, in Dolores Hidalgo, Guanajuato. title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters’ Has Led Billboard’s Top Soundtracks Chart for 58 Weeks: Only One Soundtrack Has Led Longer (Full List)
summary: Will the K-pop megahit take the lead? We'll soon see.
body: KPop Demon Hunters has slayed on Billboard ’s Top Soundtracks chart, having led the list for 58 weeks – just four weeks shy of the record. This chart was introduced a little more than 25 years ago – on June 30, 2001 – which means it doesn’t include blockbuster soundtracks of previous eras, such as West Side Story, The Sound of Music, Doctor Zhivago, Saturday Night Fever and Purple Rain . Actually, it does include one – The Vince Guaraldi Trio ’s 1965 TV soundtrack, A Charlie Brown Christmas – but only because of its chart success since 2001. KPop Demon Hunters has been No. 1 for all but four of its 62 weeks on Top Soundtracks, having yielded for one week each to Wicked: For Good , the holiday perennial A Charlie Brown Christmas , Charli xcx ’s Wuthering Heights and the soundtrack to this year’s most-talked about TV miniseries, Heated Rivalry . title: YouTube TV just finished rolling out one of its biggest new perks
summary: The ESPN Unlimited upgrade is now complete.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR ESPN Unlimited is now fully integrated into YouTube TV. Eligible subscribers can watch its content without switching to the ESPN app. The integration also brings features like multiview, alternate feeds, and ESPN Fantasy support. YouTube TV and ESPN have been on a bit of a rollercoaster, with last year’s Disney carriage dispute briefly taking ESPN and other channels off the service. One of the sweeteners when the two sides eventually struck a new deal was access to ESPN Unlimited for YouTube TV subscribers, and that started rolling out in August . But until now, you still had to leave YouTube TV and watch it on the ESPN app. That changes today, with ESPN Unlimited now fully integrated into YouTube TV. YouTube announced the full integration in a blog post , confirming that it applies to subscribers on the main YouTube TV plan or any plan that includes Sports. That brings events including the US Open, college football, PGA Tour golf, WWE Premium Live Events, La Liga, and out-of-market NHL games into the app, along with ESPN Originals, Films, and the full 30 for 30 library.

title: Coco Jones’ Early Success in Music: A Blessing, a Burden, or a Little Bit of Both? ‘Am I Stuck? I Don’t Know.’
summary: After “ICU” helped define her career, Coco Jones is pushing herself beyond expectations and figuring out what comes next.
body: Coco Jones is all about having the freedom to express herself as an artist. Ahead of releasing “Body So Tea” in July, Jones definitely spilled some tea about her concerns with her career and her artistry. She posted a video diary where she candidly spoke about not having her sound figured out yet, despite being crazy talented. We know Coco as a Grammy winner, a powerhouse vocalist and an artist who has been working toward this moment for years. But even with all of that, she still finds herself asking the same question: What exactly is my sound? “I never came into this game knowing exactly what I do,” she says. “I knew I could sing my ass off, that was pretty clear and that was pretty much the only consistent, but I didn’t really have a ‘thing.’ Personality? Sure. Relatable, I guess? I don’t know. Anyway, I think it’s biting me in the ass right now.” That honesty was in reference to the singles she released following her debut album, Why Not More? Coco is currently in a new album run, and I actually spoke to Jones about her debut album Why Not More? last year. title: Google Clock’s new timer UI is here, and your muscle memory won’t like it
summary: Google Clock's Timers tab just got a big makeover.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google is gradually rolling out a new UI for timers in the Clock app. The numbers are flatter and come without the circular background; there are presets for 1, 5, 10, and 15 minutes; and the start button has moved. Multiple timers now appear as a grid. Google has rolled out a few updates as part of the September Android Drop, like Guided Vision for Gemini Live and a crossover between Google Messages and Keep . Not to be missed, the company is also giving the Google Clock app some attention. Specifically, the Timers tab is going to look a little different from how you remember. In the UI you’re familiar with, the Timers tab features a large card with rounded numbers. The numbers are also rounded for the numeric keypad overlay, but these numbers are contained in a circular background. If you have more than one timer, this card gains an extra button at the bottom to close it so you can see your other timers. When there are multiple timers, they are arranged in a vertical pattern, allowing you to scroll through them.

body: Galaxy S25 Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR The Galaxy S25 is getting Samsung’s Horizontal Lock camera feature in One UI 9 Beta 1. The feature keeps the recorded video level even as you rotate or flip the phone. Horizontal Lock was previously spotted in an internal One UI 9 build for the Galaxy S25 Plus. The Galaxy S25 series has only just joined Samsung’s One UI 9 beta program , so we’re still digging around to see which new features have made the jump from the Galaxy S26. One of the better camera upgrades appears to be among them, with the Horizontal Lock apparently now working on the Galaxy S25. X user CID ( @theonecid ) shared a video of the feature running on what they identify as a Galaxy S25 with One UI 9 Beta 1. In the clip, the phone is slowly rotated all the way around while recording, but the resulting footage stays locked upright rather than rotating with the handset.

title: Homey Portal puts a physical dial on your smart home, and it looks pretty good
summary: Controlling your smart home can now feel satisfyingly old-school.
body: TL;DR Anthom has launched the Homey Portal, a new €249 smart home controller with a 2.8-inch round touchscreen and stainless-steel rotary dial for controlling lights, music, temperature, and more. The device is designed to be used by anyone in the room, with each Portal assigned to a specific zone such as the living room or kitchen. It is now up for pre-order, with shipments expected to begin before the end of the year. One of the first and most interesting smart home announcements coming out of IFA this year isn’t another smart speaker, sensor, or connected appliance. It is something quite cool and easy to use. Anthom, the company behind Homey , has announced a new device called the Homey Portal. It’s a €249 smart home controller with a small screen and a large dial that lets you control your smart home devices without reaching for your phone.

title: Your Pixel 11 will soon have a fix for the static noise ruining your videos
summary: Google confirms Pixel 11 video static noise bug, promises a fix is coming.
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Pixel 11 series users have been reporting an issue with Video Boost. The issue causes static noise to appear in videos recorded with the feature. A Google spokesperson has confirmed to Android Authority that a fix has been identified and a rollout will come in the following weeks. The Pixel 11 series just recently launched, and it’s stumbling out of the gate with a video recording problem. If you’ve noticed noisy static in your recordings, you’re not alone. As Android Authority reported last week, a number of buyers have been experiencing this problem. Fortunately, it may not be long before a fix arrives. To quickly summarize the situation, we spotted reports on Reddit that suggested there was an issue with Video Boost (a Pixel camera feature that enhances video color, lighting, stabilization, and low-light detail). According to the reports, videos captured with this feature on contained static noise. The cause of the issue is unknown, but some attributed it to an Audio Zoom (a feature that boosts the sound of the zoomed-in subject while cutting down background noise) bug.

title: Take a look: Users are now getting Android’s convoluted sideloading process, and everyone hates it
summary: Android owners are getting Google's new sideloading process, and new screenshots give us an even closer look.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR At least one Android device owner has received the advanced flow for sideloading apps. The user shared screenshots outlining the process, covering the 24-hour wait and more. Fellow users expressed frustration with this change, while our own poll earlier this year also revealed widespread opposition. Google announced a couple of weeks ago that it had started rolling out its advanced flow for sideloading apps on Android devices. This controversial new process requires users to restart their phones and then wait 24 hours before they can sideload apps, and a user has shared screenshots of this new flow. Redditor Super-Ad8814 recently received the new sideloading flow on their unidentified Android device. A shared screenshot (see first image below) indeed shows that you need to confirm whether someone asked you to allow sideloading. This section also informs users that scammers often tell victims to sideload apps. Google’s fine print adds that government employees and legitimate business representatives will never ask you to enable sideloading.

title: Android Auto could soon get its own Quick Settings tiles, one toggle at a time
summary: Android Auto could soon make it easier to reach Settings options without digging through menus.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing Android-style Quick Settings in Android Auto. These Quick Settings tiles appear at the top of Android Auto notifications. They currently offer only a single control for DND, but we expect more to be added soon. Google has already made bold claims about a major Android Auto redesign and promised to deliver it by the end of the year. The refresh brings a borderless design that adapts better to a variety of screen shapes, widget support, and a media player that doesn’t hog more space than it needs. These changes make the Android Auto interface comparable to Apple’s CarPlay and are expected to roll out in batches through the end of the year. While we await the big redesign, Google is experimenting with smaller changes, including the new Android Auto icon it quietly switched to earlier today. Along with it, Google is also testing new Android Auto features, and we dug them up for you.

title: Google’s new Extreme Charging on the Pixel 11 Pro XL has a heat problem
summary: Is being 5 minutes faster really worth the higher temperatures?
body: Getting the new Pixel 11 Pro XL to fast charge as quickly as Google claims is no easy feat. First, you need to grab yourself a 45W USB PD PPS charger that supports 21V for this specific protocol. Not a hugely tall order, but it might require buying a new charger, even if you have a relatively new PPS model that only supports 11V. Secondly, there’s a new option to toggle Google’s Extreme Charging capability, which promises to shave up to five minutes off your charging needs, but you’ll need some good fortune to get it to work. In a classic Google move, Extreme Charging isn’t available right out of the box. I still haven’t figured out the exact spell required to spring into life. In my experience, the Extreme Charging settings option appeared after charging the Pixel 11 Pro XL from empty to full twice and then simply waiting for it to show up. In any case, with the feature finally unlocked, I’ve been able to test the pros and cons of the latest Pixel’s boosted charging capabilities.

There’s Gemini in Gmail, Chrome , and of course, Google Drive. This time around, though, Gemini has literally slid into our DMs, as the AI automatically appears in Google Messages — and has for some time now. But if you don’t want the shortcut to hover above your chat button, there’s at least a way to get rid of it.

title: Gemini could finally let you use your phone while it thinks about what to say
summary: Gemini could finally stop hogging your screen while it's thinking.
body: TL;DR Google has been working on a new feature that will automatically minimize the Gemini overlay while it processes a user request. It could allow people to use their phones normally while Gemini is processing their request. Google was also working on a minimize button for Gemini a few months ago, but that hasn’t been rolled out yet. Gemini can be very helpful, especially as a floating overlay that pops up when you long-press the power button. However, that overlay doesn’t let users do anything else on their phones while Gemini is running. Fortunately, Google seems to be testing a new behavior for the Gemini overlay that could be immensely helpful. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: The Galaxy S26 FE is the wrong Samsung phone to buy right now
summary: The S26 FE seems fine, but that's not enough.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority Not content with launching three foldables and a pair of smartwatches this summer, Samsung is rounding off its latest launch window with the Galaxy S26 FE . It’s hard to object to the idea behind the FE — the core of a premium Samsung phone experience with some bits trimmed off to make it easier on your bank account. And I am fairly sure that when the Galaxy S26 FE is reviewed, it will score well. But it’s still going to be a phone that’s hard to find a suitable buyer for, due to its unfortunate mix of features and pricing.

title: Apple’s first folding iPhone won’t kill Android foldables — it will save them
summary: Apple could finally make foldables cool.
body: We’re fast approaching a decade since the first commercially available foldable phones arrived — yes, I’m counting the hilariously bad Royole FlexPai. Yet, despite the strides we’ve made in the technology behind them, foldables as a category are stuck behind a proverbial wall. Everyone from Samsung to Google, Motorola, and a plethora of Chinese OEMs have spent years redesigning hinges, improving displays, and offering increasingly aggressive trade-in deals to spur take-up. Despite that, foldables still make up just 1.6% of global smartphone shipments.

title: Gemini Live’s latest upgrade makes talking across languages easier
summary: A small UI tweak brings a surprisingly useful new capability.
body: TL;DR Google is refining Gemini Live’s redesigned Android interface with another small UI change. A new live translation option is rolling out, letting Gemini translate conversations between languages in real time. The update appears to be a gradual server-side rollout, with some devices getting the refreshed UI before the translation feature arrives. For most of its existence, Gemini Live’s interface barely changed. That shifted in April when Google began testing a redesign that ditched the dedicated full-screen experience. Now, Google appears to be quietly refining that experience again, and the latest change could be much more useful than another visual refresh. A new “Turn on live translation” option appears to be rolling out to some users, enabling Gemini Live to translate conversations between languages in real time.

title: Google TV Streamer just got a 50% price hike, but here’s how you can get it at the older price
summary: The older price still exists at a few places — but only until current stocks last.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google has increased the price of its TV Streamer 4K by 50%. It pegs the increase to rising component costs. Along with the Streamer, Google is also hiking prices for certain models of the Nest Cam and doorbells. The Google TV Streamer 4K , launched in 2024, is one of the most capable devices for converting any screen or an older dumb LCD or plasma TV into a smart TV. The Streamer’s 4GB RAM provides ample headroom for the ad-ridden Google TV homepage to load and scroll very easily, while offering bragging rights for the quickest Google TV updates. However, that bigger-than-others RAM is now adding to Google’s manufacturing bills (thanks to AI-driven RAM and storage shortages), and it’s being passed on to consumers. Google’s streaming hardware, which was selling at a 25% discount back in July , is now seeing a sharp 50% price hike. With this change, the TV Streamer, launched in 2024, is now available for $149.99 — up from $99.99. The prices have already been updated at the Google Store and Best Buy, but Amazon and Walmart continue to sell remaining units at the older price.

title: Android Auto gets a fresh new icon before its big redesign
summary: Google is ditching long-standing blue for green.
body: Credit: Dhruv Bhutani / Android Authority TL;DR Ahead of the big Android Auto redesign, the app is getting a new icon. Android Auto ditches the blue icon for a green one. The new icon also features rounder corners than before. Android Auto is set to receive a major makeover in the coming months, with more fluid elements, fewer rigid shapes, widget support, and video playback — finally ! So anyone who still considers Android Auto inferior (at least, visually) to Apple CarPlay will no longer have their reasons to complain. The exact date for this rollout remains unclear at this moment, but with Google having crossed major milestones in terms of hardware launches — though the Googlebook launch still remains, we could expect it to pour its energy into bringing the promised software upgrades. title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 is selling so well, Samsung is borrowing parts from the future
summary: The company is reportedly using future component reserves to fill the gap.
body: TL;DR Galaxy Z Fold 8 demand is reportedly outpacing Samsung’s expectations. A Display Driver IC (DDI) shortage is now putting pressure on Fold 8 production. Samsung is tapping future DDI reserves to keep making current Fold 8 units. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra just became the best-selling Android phone globally in Q2 2026, while the regular Galaxy S26 also cracked the top 10. Now, Samsung has another phone that people apparently want more than it expected — so much so that the company is reportedly dipping into component stock reserved for future production to keep the Galaxy Z Fold 8 coming. According to ZDNet Korea , Samsung is running short of the Display Driver IC (DDI) used to control the pixels on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 OLED display. Samsung has reportedly increased its component orders after demand for the passport-style foldable exceeded expectations. But its DDI supplier, Taiwan’s United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC), has little room to ramp up production.

title: New Android 17 QPR2 feature lets you peek inside your phone’s secure sandbox
summary: Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 introduces new Private Compute Core data logging controls inside Privacy Dashboard.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 adds a dedicated “Data logging” menu for Private Compute Core within Privacy Dashboard. Users can toggle logging between Limited (up to three days/100MB) and Detailed (up to 12 hours/100MB) tiers, download logs, or delete them. Google rolled out Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , and alongside several under-the-hood tweaks, it introduces a major transparency upgrade for how the OS handles sensitive on-device data. The new release adds a dedicated “Data logging” section for the Private Compute Core right inside Privacy Dashboard. Private Compute Core is Android’s isolated sandbox that powers machine learning features such as Live Caption, Now Playing, and Smart Reply, without exposing user data directly to the cloud or other apps. While Private Compute Core has historically operated in a secure silo, this new Privacy Dashboard entry in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 lets users actively monitor, log, and review any outbound data leaving the Private Compute Core environment.

A lot of us look at the phone we have now, and if we liked it, we look for the newest version of the same thing: probably more powerful, likely introducing a couple new features, and hopefully not costing too much more. But the market doesn’t always make things so simple for us, and this year with Google’s new Pixel 11 series, some shoppers might want to take a long, hard look at exactly what those upgrades offer — and what Google wants us to pay for them. This year’s Pixel 11 Pro phones can feel a little underwhelming depending on your expectations, but what are shoppers supposed to do about it? Waiting in a parked car while someone runs into a shop is hardly the most exciting way to spend a few minutes. That familiar scenario apparently gave the developer behind Android Auto app Xtream Player an idea: why not put a few simple games on the dashboard for those moments when the car isn’t moving? That idea is now part of Xtream Player v1.4.0, which also brings new icons, YouTube Music improvements, and playback fixes. title: Google Messages has a bizarre bug that’s sending old texts to random people
summary: Old conversations are allegedly resurfacing in places they definitely shouldn’t.
body: TL;DR Some Google Messages users say old texts from unrelated conversations are unexpectedly resurfacing. Reports span multiple Pixel and Samsung phones. In some cases, those messages appear to be sent alongside new texts or images, raising serious privacy concerns. Google Messages is getting some welcome attention with custom chat themes and selective text copying finally becoming available, but the app’s recent run of bugs is taking some shine off those additions. Besides broken RCS messaging and conversations turning into multiple threads , users are reporting a more worrying problem: Messages appears to be pulling old texts from unrelated conversations and attaching or sending them with new messages. Several Reddit reports describe the same basic nightmare. A user starts a new conversation, only for Messages to insert a message from a completely different chat, sometimes from months or even years ago. In some cases, the stray text appears alongside a photo or group message. In others, users say the old message actually reaches the unintended recipient.

title: I lived with Samsung’s worst 2025 Android phone for a year. Here’s why I’m finally giving up

body: Three months after Samsung launched the three mainline Galaxy S25 models, it followed up with a fourth offering: the Galaxy S25 Edge. The Galaxy S25 Edge came with better specs and fewer compromises than the iPhone Air, but one year later, Samsung’s slim flagship has no successor in sight. It’s easily the brand’s worst phone of 2025, and seems destined to be forgotten as a quirky flop. I bought the Samsung Galaxy S25 Edge in cash, with no promotions or discounts, and used it for the last year. Whenever I wasn’t reviewing a new Android phone, the Galaxy S25 Edge was my daily driver. title: Your Pixel’s built-in PA system is finally easy to find in Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4
summary: The latest Android 17 QPR2 Beta makes Samsung Galaxy-like Voice broadcast feature easier to activate.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4, which was released last week, brings an easier way to broadcast your voice over a private network. The new Audio broadcast feature expands Pixels’ existing Auracast-based media-sharing features to transmit audio over Bluetooth LE Audio. While the feature was introduced last month, it is now much easier to access. Google is in the final legs of testing Android 17 QPR2 Beta before a significant feature drop for Pixels in September. Last Friday, it released the fourth QPR2 Beta, sorting out a long list of bugs and usability issues from previous beta builds. As part of Android 17 QPR2 Beta 4 , Google is adding a few useful features that didn’t make it into the changelog, including easier access to Voice Broadcast. Voice Broadcast on Pixel devices with Android 17 QPR2 Beta is like a personal PA system. It lets users voice their views over, or share audio from a media player, in private listening channels. This private network is enabled by Bluetooth LE (Low Energy), and audio devices — earbuds and such — used by recipients must support the technology.

title: Lake Ontario is now ‘Lake America’ on Google Maps, but not for everyone

body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google Maps is now starting to call Lake Ontario “Lake America” following recent executive orders. Last week, President Trump signed the executive order to rename the lake officially. Google says the new change is only visible for people in the US, while those in Canada will continue to see “Lake Ontario.” Last week, US President Donald Trump signed executive orders to officially rename Lake Ontario “Lake America,” his second re-christening, so to speak, of a body of water after the Gulf of Mexico . Following these official orders, Google Maps has started showing the name of the body of water bordering both the US and Canada. In an official announcement , Google noted it will start showing the lake’s new official name, as designated by the US Geographic Names Information System (GNIS). It said the official name change will appear on Google Maps, but only for people in the US.

I’d immediately pick up my phone and check what I’d missed. Smartphones have mostly left that idea behind. That’s why Google’s HiLight feature on the Pixel 11 Pro series immediately caught my attention. It feels like a much more modern take on the notification LED I used to love.
